The season ran from 19 February to 31 October 2010. [[Atlético Petróleos de Luanda|Petro Atlético]] were the defending champions. The league comprised 16 teams and the bottom three were relegated to the 2011 [[Gira Angola]].{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/ango2011.html |title=Angola 2011 |date=May 6, 2011 |access-date=May 20, 2011 |author=King, Ian}} [[G.D. Interclube|Interclube]] were crowned champions, while [[C.D. Huíla|Desportivo da Huíla]], [[Sporting Clube Petróleos de Cabinda|Sporting de Cabinda]] and [[S.L. Benfica (Lubango)|Benfica do Lubango]] were relegated.{{cite web |url=http://www.portalangop.co.ao/angola/en_us/noticias/desporto/2010/10/44/Interclube-win-national-first-division-football-championship,1f3e4cd6-f9cf-43d5-933a-3b449d57d217.html |title=Interclube win national first division football championship |publisher=ANGOP.com |date= 1 Nov 2010 |access-date= 7 Sep 2015}} [[Daniel Mpele Mpele]] of [[Kabuscorp S.C.P.|Kabuscorp]] finished as top scorer with 14 goals.{{cite web |url=http://www.fafutebol-angola.og.ao/noticias/noticias.php?id=468 |title=Love sagra-se melhor "artilheiro" pela terceira vez |date=September 6, 2011 |publisher=Federação Angolana de Futebol |access-date=2013-05-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120122135633/http://www.fafutebol-angola.og.ao/noticias/noticias.php?id=468 |archive-date=2012-01-22 |url-status=dead }} ==Changes from 2010 season== '''Relegated:''' [[Académica Petróleos do Lobito|Académica do Lobito]], [[Estrela Clube Primeiro de Maio|Primeiro de Maio]]
